citation: G. W. Bewick, "Fast Multiplication: Algorithms and Implementation", PhD dissertation, Stanford University, CSL-TR-94-617, 1994
title: FAST MULTIPLICATION: ALGORITHMS AND IMPLEMENTATION

segments.title: Front matter
segments.why: The front matter contains only publication metadata, approvals, acknowledgments, and a summary of material developed in later chapters.

segments.title: Introduction
segments.why: The introduction surveys binary multiplier architectures and implementation tradeoffs before the detailed treatment.

segments.title: Generating Partial Products
segments.why: The chapter defines conventional and higher-radix Booth recoding and develops partially redundant hard-multiple generation.

segments.title: Adders for Multiplication
segments.why: The chapter derives and compares high-speed carry-propagate structures used for hard multiples and final multiplier assimilation.

segments.title: Implementing Multipliers
segments.why: The chapter describes the construction and physical optimization of Booth/non-Booth partial-product generators and carry-save summation networks.

segments.title: Exploring the Design Space
segments.why: The chapter evaluates complete multiplier organizations and their final carry-propagate adders by latency, area, and power.

segments.title: Conclusions
segments.why: The conclusions compare Booth variants and tree/array carry-save reduction structures using measured design results.

segments.title: Sign Extension in Booth Multipliers
segments.why: The appendix derives compact sign-extension and negative-partial-product handling for Booth-recoded multipliers.

segments.title: Efficient Sticky Bit Computation
segments.why: The appendix develops hardware for computing the IEEE floating-point multiplier sticky bit without waiting for every low product bit from the final adder.

segments.title: Negative Logic Adders
segments.why: The appendix proves the positive/negative-logic equivalence used to implement alternating-polarity high-speed carry networks.

segments.title: Bibliography
segments.why: The bibliography contains citations rather than arithmetic-unit design detail.
